studies.title: Near transfer to an unrelated N-back task mediates the effect of N-back working memory training on matrix reasoning
studies.authors: Anja Pahor, Aaron R. Seitz & Susanne M. Jaeggi
studies.feature: All modes require updating and retrieval at the exact N-back interval. This work motivates checking progress on unfamiliar updating tasks as well as on the practised game.
studies.positiveFinding: Across three randomized trials involving 460 people, performance on an untrained N-back task statistically mediated transfer to matrix reasoning. The third trial also found an intervention effect on a working-memory composite.
studies.limitation: Two of the three trials did not show an overall intervention effect on matrix reasoning. A mediation result does not mean every participant, or this game, gains intelligence. The publisher's corrected article is linked.

studies.title: Dual n-back working memory training evinces superior transfer effects compared to the method of loci
studies.authors: Wenjuan Li, Qiuzhu Zhang, Hongying Qiao, Donggang Jin, Ronald K. Ngetich, Junjun Zhang, Zhenlan Jin & Ling Li
studies.feature: Relevant to active memory updating and to distinguishing a mnemonic strategy from N-back practice. Spoken and displayed digits offer different presentations of the ordered task here.
studies.positiveFinding: In a study of 148 young adults, dual N-back and method-of-loci groups improved on their trained tasks and digit span. The N-back group also showed faster responses on the highest-load change-detection condition; this was a response-speed result rather than a training-specific accuracy gain.
studies.limitation: The outcomes were memory tasks, not a demonstrated general-intelligence gain. Dual audiovisual N-back differs from ordered digits, and method-of-loci training is not the same as the Da Vinci method.

studies.title: Working memory training revisited: A multi-level meta-analysis of n-back training studies
studies.authors: Anna Soveri, Jan Antfolk, Linda Karlsson, Benny Salo & Matti Laine
studies.feature: Supports N-back as a trainable updating skill and the value of testing an unpractised N-back format. It helps distinguish better game performance from broader transfer.
studies.positiveFinding: A synthesis of 33 randomized controlled studies found a medium-sized benefit on untrained N-back tasks. Smaller benefits appeared on other working-memory measures. The main analysis also found a small positive fluid-intelligence effect (g = 0.16); its significance depended on the analysis, as described below.
studies.limitation: Transfer to fluid intelligence and cognitive control was very small; fluid-intelligence transfer was not significant after the reported control-group adjustment. Most transfer was specific to N-back-like tasks.

studies.title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory: a meta-analysis
studies.authors: Jacky Au, Ellen Sheehan, Nancy Tsai, Greg J. Duncan, Martin Buschkuehl & Susanne M. Jaeggi
studies.feature: Provides a positive research rationale for exploring whether repeated N-back updating can support reasoning beyond the exact trained stimuli.
studies.positiveFinding: Across 20 N-back training studies in healthy adults, the authors found a small, statistically significant average benefit on fluid-intelligence tests.
studies.limitation: This pooled estimate is not a promised IQ increase. Study design and analysis choices matter, and later syntheses such as Soveri et al. found much stronger near transfer than far transfer. No included study tested Ontological Worlds.

studies.title: On the impacts of working memory training on executive functioning
studies.authors: Tiina Salminen, Tilo Strobach & Torsten Schubert
studies.feature: Relates to replacing old information, selecting the correct remembered trial and maintaining task rules despite competing stimuli. The studied task combined auditory letters and visual locations.
studies.positiveFinding: After 14 sessions of dual N-back practice, young adults improved on a separate updating task, aspects of task switching and attentional processing.
studies.limitation: This small study used a passive control group. It found no transfer to its reasoning measure or separate dual-task test. Its auditory and visual streams are not equivalent to the game's multiple ordered digits.

studies.title: Short- and long-term benefits of cognitive training
studies.authors: Susanne M. Jaeggi, Martin Buschkuehl, John Jonides & Priti Shah
studies.feature: Motivates attending to the quality of learning during adaptive practice, rather than assuming that completing sessions alone guarantees transfer.
studies.positiveFinding: In children given game-like working-memory practice, those with substantial training improvement also improved on untrained reasoning tests relative to an active comparison group. The pattern remained at a three-month follow-up.
studies.limitation: The positive result depended on training-gain subgroups rather than a universal benefit. It does not establish the best difficulty threshold, predict a particular user's outcome, or validate this ordered-digit task.

studies.title: Hundred Days of Cognitive Training Enhance Broad Cognitive Abilities in Adulthood: Findings from the COGITO Study
studies.authors: Florian Schmiedek, Martin Lövdén & Ulman Lindenberger
studies.feature: Supports evaluating progress across several different tasks and ability measures. Varied assessment is more informative than a single personal-best game score.
studies.positiveFinding: Younger and older adults completed an extensive programme combining perceptual-speed, working-memory and episodic-memory practice. Positive transfer was found on untrained tests and on broader ability factors.
studies.limitation: The programme involved more than 100 one-hour sessions and many tasks. It cannot show that short N-back sessions, one isolated component, or this particular game produce the same changes.

studies.title: Transfer of learning after updating training mediated by the striatum
studies.authors: Erika Dahlin, Anna Stigsdotter Neely, Anne Larsson, Lars Bäckman & Lars Nyberg
studies.feature: Relevant to the updating operation shared by the modes: keep the relevant information available, replace outdated information and retrieve from the correct temporal position.
studies.positiveFinding: Five weeks of updating practice transferred to an untrained 3-back task. The trained and transfer tasks shared a training-related change in striatal activity.
studies.limitation: Transfer did not extend to a task lacking the shared updating demand, and age-related differences constrained it. Shared brain activity is a mechanism clue, not proof of broad intelligence improvement.

studies.title: Improving fluid intelligence with training on working memory
studies.authors: Susanne M. Jaeggi, Martin Buschkuehl, John Jonides & Walter J. Perrig
studies.feature: An early positive test of adaptive N-back practice using simultaneous auditory letters and visual positions. It motivates the possibility of updating-based transfer while preserving the need to test it independently.
studies.positiveFinding: The authors reported gains on fluid-reasoning measures after dual N-back training, with larger reported gains in groups assigned more training.
studies.limitation: This early finding does not settle the wider mixed literature or establish benefits for ordered digits. The game's spoken sequence and position rule differ from the dual audiovisual task used in the study.

studies.title: Updating, Fast and Slow: Items, but Not Item-Context Bindings, are Quickly Updated Into Working Memory as Part of Response Selection
studies.authors: Yoav Kessler, Nitzan Zilberman & Shalva Kvitelashvili
studies.feature: Remember both the content and its place: which digit belongs in each ordered slot, which trial is N steps back, and which descriptor belongs to which entity or endpoint. These are bindings, not simply a bag of familiar items.
studies.positiveFinding: Experiments distinguished rapidly updating a single item from updating two items tied to different contexts. The latter incurred a response-time cost; the single-item updating benefit was replicated. This provides a precise mechanism rationale for practicing item-to-context associations, including the current-versus-previous roles required even in 1-back.
studies.limitation: This was a laboratory mechanism study, not a training intervention. It does not establish that increasing item count or ontology complexity produces greater intelligence gains. The extension from screen-position bindings to semantic endpoint roles is a design inference.

studies.title: Working memory updating training promotes plasticity & behavioural gains: A systematic review & meta-analysis
studies.authors: Katerina Pappa, Viveka Biswas, Kristin E. Flegal, Jonathan J. Evans & Satu Baylan
studies.feature: All three areas repeatedly replace outdated information while retaining the relevant trial. This synthesis connects that updating practice to measurable learning, related-task transfer and neural plasticity.
studies.positiveFinding: A review of adult updating-training studies with brain imaging found large improvements on trained tasks. In the eligible neuroimaging-study subset, transfer to related tasks was moderate (Hedges' g = 0.63). The neural review found recurring decreases in frontoparietal task activity, consistent with changes in how practiced processing is implemented.
studies.limitation: Far transfer was small and not statistically significant (g = 0.15). Study quality was generally modest, and the synthesis selected studies with imaging. A brain-activity change is not itself an IQ increase or evidence that lower activity is always better.

studies.title: Working memory updating involves item-specific removal
studies.authors: Ullrich K. H. Ecker, Klaus Oberauer & Stephan Lewandowsky
studies.feature: As the remembered sequence advances, retire the obsolete trial while retaining the trials still needed. In Mode 2, keep separate the operation of updating a remembered world and the operation of comparing its stable internal bindings.
studies.positiveFinding: Three experiments provided evidence for active removal of outdated working-memory information. Removal operated on particular items, and updating only part of a memory set involved switching between maintenance and updating. This identifies a useful control operation to practice: replacing what has become irrelevant without losing what remains relevant.
studies.limitation: The study tested how updating works, not whether a training course improves it. N-back advances a temporal sequence rather than using the study's exact partial-update procedure; training transfer is a proposed application.

studies.title: Spaced cognitive training promotes training transfer
studies.authors: Zuowei Wang, Renlai Zhou & Priti Shah
studies.feature: A rationale for returning to practice across days. The running-span task required continuously updating the latest three items and preserving their order, closely connecting scheduling to ordered-memory practice.
studies.positiveFinding: The researchers randomized 115 fifth-graders, with 95 included in analysis, to equal amounts of updating practice distributed over 2, 5, 10 or 20 days, or to extra mathematics instruction. The 20-day training group improved on Raven's matrices more than the active control. This supplies positive evidence that practice distribution can matter beyond total minutes.
studies.limitation: The 20-day advantage used a selected follow-up comparison and a one-tailed test; the overall spacing trend was marginal in a two-tailed test. Training groups also received rewards absent from the mathematics control. This does not establish an optimal adult schedule or how to space individual spoken digits.

studies.title: Distinct transfer effects of training different facets of working memory capacity
studies.authors: Claudia C. von Bastian & Klaus Oberauer
studies.feature: The modes combine remembering with active processing, and Mode 2 also requires selecting the relevant level and role. This study motivates identifying those operations separately when examining what improves.
studies.positiveFinding: In a randomized study with an active perceptual-matching control and 121 analyzed adults, participants practiced one working-memory component for 20 sessions. Storage-plus-processing training improved reasoning, with some evidence of working-memory transfer; supervisory task-switching training transferred to switching and reasoning. Different practiced operations produced different patterns of benefit.
studies.limitation: The relational-integration group did not show comparable broad transfer. The study therefore supports specific storage/processing and control ingredients, rather than proving that all relational complexity helps. Its three-task training packages differ from the modes, and switching world scope is not identical to experimentally switching task rules.

studies.title: Control of interference during working memory updating
studies.authors: Arnaud Szmalec, Frederick Verbruggen, André Vandierendonck & Eva Kemps
studies.feature: Reject a familiar item from the wrong trial or slot. In Mode 2, the analogous challenge is rejecting familiar category words when their endpoint attachments are wrong; in Mode 1, a familiar direction must still belong to the correctly aligned relation.
studies.positiveFinding: Four N-back experiments distinguished familiarity from recollection of an item's correct context. Even semantically related, previously unseen items could create interference. Encountering interference prompted immediate behavioral adjustments favoring context-sensitive recollection. This gives a concrete rationale for lures that require checking precise bindings instead of answering from familiarity alone.
studies.limitation: These were immediate task effects, not evidence of lasting training transfer. The study's temporal and semantic lures differ from the game's slot and ontology-role lures; more interference is not automatically better practice.

studies.title: Dual n-back training increases the capacity of the focus of attention
studies.authors: Lilienthal, L., Tamez, E., Shelton, J. T., Myerson, J., & Hale, S.
studies.feature: Keep recent items available while the comparison window advances. The N-back level changes how far back the relevant trial lies; this study connects performance-adjusted practice with a separate measure of retaining an updating sequence.
studies.positiveFinding: Adaptive dual N-back training improved an untrained running-span task, whereas fixed-load N-back practice and a no-contact control did not. The authors interpreted this selective transfer as increased capacity of the focus of attention. The result gives a specific positive target beyond a better score on the practised N-back task.
studies.limitation: Other measures of the proposed working-memory mechanisms showed no differential improvement. The comparison concerned adaptive dual N-back; this game's user-selected level and multiple ordered digits use a different format.

studies.title: Neural effects of short-term training on working memory
studies.authors: Buschkuehl, M., Hernandez-Garcia, L., Jaeggi, S. M., Bernard, J. A., & Jonides, J.
studies.feature: Preserve the update-and-compare operation when presentation changes. The game's displayed and spoken digits offer a practical connection: check the same exact-N and same-slot rule using different sensory access to the sequence.
studies.positiveFinding: After approximately twenty minutes of adaptive visual-location N-back practice daily for seven days, the training group improved on an untrained auditory-letter N-back task relative to an active vocabulary/general-knowledge control. This cross-modal result supports investigating whether practiced updating can remain useful when the stimulus format changes.
studies.limitation: Fifty-five participants were analyzed; group allocation was largely sequential rather than random. Auditory transfer was strongest at 3-back, the only separately significant load. The demonstrated transfer concerned the N-back update-and-compare operation across visual-location and auditory-letter stimuli.

studies.title: The early effects of external and internal strategies on working memory updating training
studies.authors: Laine, M., Fellman, D., Waris, O., & Nyman, T. J.
studies.feature: Practice an explicit way to organize and compare the sequence, preserving which item belongs to which remembered position. Then examine whether that strategy works with unfamiliar stimuli.
studies.positiveFinding: In a preregistered randomized trial with 116 adults, one thirty-minute digit N-back session with strategy instruction improved subsequent letter and color 3-back discrimination compared with identical practice without instruction and passive controls.
studies.limitation: Benefits concerned accuracy on harder N-back variants; reaction times and structurally different memory tasks showed no reliable advantage. The experiment studied single-item N-back, while this game's ordered trials can contain several digits.

studies.title: Transfer of working memory training to the inhibitory control of auditory distraction
studies.authors: Kattner, F.
studies.feature: Distinguish updating from controlling a competing response. This provides a research direction for the game's interference settings: identify the particular control operation being challenged.
studies.positiveFinding: In a randomized study of 74 analyzed participants, eight sessions of inhibitory dual N-back reduced disruption from irrelevant speech during serial recall more than standard dual N-back and a passive control. The modified task required withholding frequent responses when an N-back match appeared.
studies.limitation: Training lasted up to eighty minutes per session. Its reversed response rule differs from this game's lures. Transfer did not extend to Simon-task interference, task switching or fluid-intelligence scores.

studies.title: Transfer after Working Memory Updating Training
studies.authors: Waris, O., Soveri, A., & Laine, M.
studies.feature: Identify the operations shared across practice formats: maintaining order, replacing outdated contents and checking an earlier item. These provide concrete links between ordered N-back and other updating exercises.
studies.positiveFinding: Thirty-one adults were randomized to three updating tasks or commercial-game practice for five weeks. Updating training improved an untrained numerical N-back task, a running-memory composite and backward-span performance. The authors linked the transfer pattern to operations shared across tasks.
studies.limitation: The small study combined selective updating, moving-object tracking and dual N-back, so individual contributions cannot be isolated. Passive storage, dual-task performance and fluid-intelligence scores showed no reliable transfer.
